steps.en: What you see: The septum thickens asymmetrically while the cavity stays small. A wall of 15 mm or more at end diastole confirms the diagnosis, with 13 to 14 mm borderline when family history or gene carrier status supports it. The left atrium enlarges from diastolic dysfunction and tissue Doppler shows low annular velocities with a raised filling pattern. Apical variants show giant negative T waves with an obliterated apex, and some hearts show crypts or an apical aneurysm.

Normal values with units: Maximal wall thickness. Normal about 6 to 10 mm. Borderline 13 to 14 mm with family support. Definite 15 mm or more. Marked 20 mm or more carries high sudden death risk markers.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on left ventricular wall thickness
Septal to posterior wall ratio. Above 1.3 with a small cavity supports asymmetric disease over athlete heart or pressure load.. Source: BSE minimum dataset, section on left ventricular wall thickness

Resting outflow gradient. Below 30 mmHg at rest defines the non obstructive entry. Provocation above 30 mmHg reclassifies the patient.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on Doppler and haemodynamics

Filling pressure estimate. Average E to e prime above 14 with left atrial volume index above 34 ml per sq m marks raised filling pressure.. Source: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function guideline, section on filling pressures
ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Deep narrow septal Q waves in lateral leads mark septal fibrosis. Voltage criteria for hypertrophy are often met. Giant negative T waves flag the apical variant.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: A soft ejection systolic murmur eases with squatting in non obstructive disease. A fourth sound marks the stiff ventricle. The second sound may split in some patients.

What to report: Maximal thickness with position, ratio and the views measured
Resting gradient with the provocation result and method
Diastolic grade, left atrial volume index and any apical aneurysm or crypts
Family history, symptoms and athletic status for the sudden death risk discussion on referral
Red flags needing urgent referral: Unexplained syncope with marked thickness 20 mm or more, needs urgent inherited cardiac conditions review
Family sudden death with borderline thickness in a first degree relative, needs urgent family screening
Apical aneurysm with thrombus or ventricular arrhythmia, needs urgent rhythm and anticoagulation review
Pitfalls: Athlete heart stays below 13 mm with a large cavity and normal diastolic indices, so record training load.
Hypertensive disease is concentric with a normal ratio, so compute the ratio in every thick wall.
Genotype positive relatives can show crypts before hypertrophy, so screen families even with normal thickness.

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start in the parasternal long axis and freeze at end diastole on the R wave.
Measure maximal septal thickness perpendicular to the wall, excluding trabeculation and false tendons.
Measure posterior wall thickness at the same level and compute the asymmetry ratio.
Move to short axis at mitral, papillary and apical levels and map every segment.
Record resting outflow gradient with continuous wave Doppler, then tissue Doppler and left atrial volume for diastolic grade.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Including trabeculation or an oblique cut that overreads thickness. Fix: Turn gain down and measure the compact wall only on a perpendicular beam.
Missing apical hypertrophy by scanning basal planes only. Fix: Map all three short axis levels plus the apex. Apical disease hides from the long axis alone.
Calling disease non obstructive from resting gradients alone. Fix: Withhold the label until provocation is done, since obstruction appears only on standing or Valsalva in one third of patients.

remember.en: Grade diastole quantitatively and flag sudden death risk markers for referral.

o.en: 15 mm or more at end diastole

why.en: Definite disease needs 15 mm or more, with 13 to 14 mm borderline when family or gene evidence supports it.

q.en: Resting gradient is 12 mmHg. How is the non obstructive label earned?

o.en: Below 30 mmHg at rest with provocation testing still required

why.en: Resting gradient below 30 mmHg defines the entry, but provocation with Valsalva or standing is still required.

q.en: Which pattern separates HCM from hypertensive disease?

o.en: Concentric thickening with a normal ratio
A large cavity with thin walls
Asymmetric thickening with ratio above 1.3 and a small cavity

why.en: Asymmetry with a ratio above 1.3 and a small cavity marks HCM against concentric pressure load.

q.en: An apical aneurysm is found with ventricular ectopy. What next?

o.en: Urgent inherited cardiac conditions review with family screening
Reassurance that apical variants never clot

why.en: Apical aneurysms carry arrhythmic and thrombotic risk and need urgent specialist review with family screening.

q.en: Which pair quantifies raised filling pressure here?

o.en: Average E to e prime above 14 with left atrial volume index above 34 ml per sq m

why.en: Average E to e prime above 14 with a dilated atrium is the guideline quantitative pair.
